'''Ootsu Shrine''' (大津神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Habikino|en|Habikino|qid=Q694308|lt=Habikino City}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en|Osaka Prefecture|qid=Q122723|lt=Osaka Prefecture}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and was formerly classified as a {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q134917284|qq= 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}.

== Enshrined Deities ==
* Main deities:
** {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素盞嗚尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qid=Q272993}}
** {{ill|Kushinadahime|qid=Q505469|lt=Kushinadahime-no-Mikoto|ja|奇稻田姫命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kushinadahime|qid=Q505469}}
** {{ill|Otori-sama|ja|天日鷲命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Hiwashi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天日鷲神|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10939697}}
* Secondary deities:
** {{ill|Oyamakui no Kami|qid=Q10935105|lt=Ōyamakui-no-Mikoto|ja|大山咋命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oyamakui no Kami|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大山咋神|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10935105}}
** {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|ja|Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugawara no Michizane|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q382005}}

== History ==
The shrine's founding is traditionally attributed to the 6th century. However, it is recorded in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|lt=Engishiki Jinmyō-chō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|qq=}} compiled during Emperor Daigo’s reign in the early 10th century as "Ootsu Shrine, three seats, Kuwari, and Yoroi" in the {{ill|Kawachi Province|en|Kawachi Province|qid=Q1047150|lt=Kawachi Province}} {{ill|Tajihinokōri district|ja|丹比郡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanpi District|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11368538}}. It has long been known as "The Grand Shrine of Tange no Sato."<ref name="History">[https://www.otsujinja.net/ Ootsu Shrine Official Website - History]</ref>.

In ancient times, this area was dominated by three clans—{{ill|Geungusu of Baekje|en|Geungusu of Baekje|qid=Q497625|lt=Geungusu of Baekje}}’s descendants: the Kazuraki, Funashi, and Tsu clans. The Tsu clan established the shrine in this area, naming the mountain "Ōmiya Mountain" and enshrining their guardian deity.<ref name="History"/>

While originally serving as the guardian shrine for the Tsu clan, their relocation to the {{ill|Yamato Province|en|Yamato Province|qid=Q907495|lt=Yamato Province}} and the decline of the {{ill|Uji-Kabane system|ja|氏姓制度|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Uji-Kabane system|qq=}} led to the shrine becoming a regional guardian for nine villages. During the rise of Buddhism, the shrine adopted the name "Gozu Tennō Shrine" and incorporated Buddhist elements, establishing a Shingon sect temple, Nanno Bō, within its grounds.<ref name="History"/>.

In the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period}}, Shinto-Buddhist syncretism was prohibited, and the temple was abolished. The shrine was renamed Ootsu Shrine in 1872 and designated as a {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q134917284|qq= 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}.<ref name="History"/>. 

Following the {{ill|Pacific War|en|Pacific War|qid=Q184425|lt=Pacific War}}, the shrine became a religious corporation under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|en|Association of Shinto Shrines|qid=Q908077|lt=Association of Shinto Shrines}} in 1946.<ref name="History"/>.

Today, it is revered as the guardian deity for western and southwestern {{ill|Habikino|en|Habikino|qid=Q694308|lt=Habikino City}}, offering blessings for disaster prevention, safe childbirth, and household safety.

== Precincts ==
* Main Shrine (designated {{ill|Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Cultural Property (Japan)|qid=Q858308|lt=Cultural property}} of {{ill|Habikino|en|Habikino|qid=Q694308|lt=Habikino City}}) - Rebuilt in 1640 (Kan'ei 17)<ref name="Habikino">[https://www.city.habikino.lg.jp/ 羽曳野市ホームページ 大津神社]</ref>.
* Worship Hall - Rebuilt in 1640.
* Heiden (offering hall) - Rebuilt in 1640.
* Shrine Office.

=== Subsidiary Shrines ===
* Ōmiya Benten Shrine - Dedicated to {{ill|Ichikishima-hime-no-Mikoto|ja|市杵嶋姫命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichikishima-hime-no-Mikoto||1=Ichikishima-hime|2=fr|3=Ichikishimahime|4=ja|5=イチキシマヒメ|6=zh|7=市寸島比賣命|8=ru|9=Итикишима-химэ|10=de|11=Ichikishima-hime}}. Features an octagonal Buddhist-style hall.<ref name="History"/>.
* Ōmiya Ebisu Shrine - Dedicated to {{ill|Ebisu|ja|戎大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ebisu|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. Built in 1987.<ref name="History"/>.
* Ōmiya Inari Shrine - Dedicated to {{ill|Ukanomitama|ja|宇迦之御魂大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ukanomitama|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ウカノミタマ}}. Built in 1972.<ref name="History"/>.
* Peace Shrine (Yawaragi-no-Yashiro) - Dedicated to the spirits of 278 war dead from the local community. Built in 1951 to commemorate the signing of the {{ill|Treaty of San Francisco|ja|サンフランシスコ講和条約|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/San Francisco Peace Treaty|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日本国との平和条約|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q392541}}.<ref name="History"/>.

== Cultural Properties ==
=== Habikino City Designated Cultural Properties ===
* Main Shrine, with plaques.

== Festivals ==
Two festivals are held annually, during which local roads are regulated:
* Summer Festival: Held annually on July 7–8. It attracts families but has no food stalls since 2022.
* Autumn Festival: Held annually on October 7–8, featuring portable shrines (mikoshi) and floats.

== location ==

* Osaka Prefecture, Habikino City, Takawashi 8-chome 1-2.

* Nearest bus stop: {{ill|Q11639080|ja|近鉄バス松原営業所|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kintetsu Bus|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11639080}} Takawashi Station, 1 trip on Saturdays.
